messages:
eva_support: Hey team — customer (AcmeRetail) opened an escalation: streaming responses cut off after ~65s, client reconnects then gets 401, and they're seeing doubled billing for the same prompt when the client retries. Full repro steps below. Can we triage? :eyes:

mike_ops: Thanks — can you paste the raw headers + sample curl they used? Also which ingress (CF/ALB) in front of the private deployment?

eva_support: They are on our Private deployment through a Cloudflare Worker in front of an ALB -> our origin. Sample they sent: `curl -v --no-buffer -N "https://acme.redwood.example.com/v1/stream?model=xlarge" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"`

alisha_sre: OK. From the logs I can see a keepalive/idle close on the ALB at 60s. The sequence: initial SSE stream starts, tokens emitted for ~60s, then a silent pause and ALB half-closes. Client tries to reconnect -> our edge receives new request but auth check returns 401 (token was short-lived, rotated) so client retries and eventually a duplicate request is counted by billing.

jordan_engineering: Adding details from runtime traces: the backend was still producing data after the ALB half-close, but TCP FIN from ALB caused the origin to get EPIPE when writing final chunks. The runtime didn't convert that to a graceful cancel so it retried some internal pieces which incremented billing counters for the same external request id.

eva_support: Customer also attached `tcpdump` showing `FIN` from ALB at ~61s after initial response and Cloudflare worker not sending keepalive pings. They tested with `--no-buffer` and with `-N` — behavior is same.

mike_ops: Two separate problems: 1) LB idle/half-close cutting SSE, 2) token lifetime + reconnect causing 401 + retry double-bill. Short-term workarounds: set client-side heartbeat (send a comment line `: hb\n` every 15s), or configure Cloudflare to preserve origin keepalive and disable buffering for that route. Also bump ALB idle timeout > 120s for that target group if possible.

alisha_sre: Repro steps I used locally: 
```
# reproduce against staging proxy
curl -v --no-buffer -N 'https://staging-proxy.example/v1/stream?prompt=hi&model=xlarge' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <short-lived-token>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream'
```
Then kill client after 70s and watch ALB target group logs: `target-response-time` shows last byte at ~61s and `elb_status_code` blank (connection closed).

jordan_engineering: Minimal Python reproducer (stream then force reconnect):
```
import requests
r = requests.get(url, stream=True, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer %s' % token})
for i, line in enumerate(r.iter_lines()):
  if i>100: break
  print(line)
# sleep to simulate idle
import time; time.sleep(75)
# reconnect
r2 = requests.get(url, stream=True, headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer %s' % token})
```
If token expires between r and r2, second request is 401 and client retries.

eva_support: Customer asked why we count billable tokens when retries happen. Is there a server-side dedupe using `x-request-id` or `Idempotency-Key`?

jordan_engineering: We currently increment billing on acceptance of the request (first successful auth + enqueue). If a client retries with same idempotency/request-id we don't fully dedupe streaming token consumption today because streamed tokens are emitted as we produce them. To mitigate: require/strongly recommend `Idempotency-Key` header and implement quick server-side check to see if a request with same key has already been completed within a short window — runtime action item.

mike_ops: Short-term config steps we provided to AcmeRetail: 1) Configure CF Worker route: `fetch(event.request, { cf: { originKeepaliveTimeout: 120 } })` (worker-level keepalive config or bypass proxy). 2) Set ALB target group idle timeout to 180s. 3) Add a small SSE comment heartbeat from the client or from a CDN edge transform every 20s. 4) Use a longer-lived token or refresh token on reconnect to avoid 401 mid-session.

alisha_sre: I also recommend tweaking worker response headers to disable buffering: set `Cache-Control: no-transform` and remove `Content-Length`, keep `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, and ensure `Connection: keep-alive` is preserved end-to-end. Cloudflare sometimes buffers when it thinks body is small or when transform is enabled.

eva_support: Customer tried `no-transform` but said Cloudflare was still buffering on their paid plan when the worker performed HTML transforms. They will try bypassing the worker for that route.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: Noted — creating incident ticket INF-2026-112 to track runtime billing dedupe + reconnect auth checks.

jordan_engineering: Action items (assigning owners):
- jordan_engineering: add defensive dedupe on Idempotency-Key + do not double-count tokens if identical request completed within 5 minutes (P0 for billing safety).
- alisha_sre: add metrics/alerts for `stream_econn_reset` spikes and ALB half-close rate (low overhead).
- mike_ops: compile customer-facing KB article with exact CF Worker and ALB settings + heartbeat example.

eva_support: I'll send the KB + workaround steps to AcmeRetail and ask them to test bypassing worker. Thanks all. Please update the INF ticket with progress. :thumbsup:
